15 seconds, 9:16 vertical screen, one continuous shot, realistic documentary photography style. Records the complete process of a man dropping a giant soap from a helicopter into a volcanic crater, followed by large amounts of soap bubbles rising from the volcano and flooding into the cabin.

【Characters and Props】
An adult male wearing a dark outdoor jacket, long pants, and boots, with a waist safety belt connected to the cabin anchor point, located inside the open side door of the helicopter.

The man holds a giant pink soap approximately 80cm long, 45cm wide, and 25cm thick with both arms. Rounded rectangular prism, smooth surface with slight wet reflections, clear thickness and weight. No packaging, no text.

Real seats, fixed handles, metal door frames, and floor visible inside the helicopter. The pilot remains in the front cockpit. Character, cabin, and prop appearances remain consistent throughout.

【Environment and Photography】
Daytime, natural light. Dark rough rock walls surround a wide volcanic crater, with slowly rolling orange-red magma at the bottom, and slight thermal disturbance in the air.

The helicopter hovers above the edge of the crater, with the side door facing the interior of the volcano. The composition clearly shows the positions of the man, the door, and the drop point below, maintaining consistency between drop height and actual fall time.

The camera is always held by the shooter inside the cabin, completing forward tilts, upward movements, and rotations near the side door. Wide-angle documentary composition, with small vibrations caused by rotors and natural handheld adjustments, actions clearly discernible. Natural exposure and color, retaining real textures of skin, clothing, rock walls, and metal.

【Continuous Time Sequence | 0:00–0:04 | Dropping the Giant Soap】
Shot from inside the cabin towards the side door. The man and the giant soap occupy the foreground, with the volcanic crater clearly visible through the door below.

The man presses the bottom edge of the soap against the threshold, steadies it with both hands, bends his knees to shift his center of gravity forward, and pushes the soap outward. His arms straighten as he pushes; once the soap's center of gravity crosses the threshold, his hands clearly release.

The soap leaves the cabin, accelerating downward with a slight rotation. The man withdraws his hands, steadies himself on the cabin handle, and stays in place to observe.

The camera naturally tilts forward, continuously panning down along the soap's trajectory, keeping a small section of the door frame at the edge of the frame. The soap gradually shrinks in depth, contacts the magma below, causing local churning. Present the entire falling process completely, without skipping distance or suddenly cutting to a close-up of the landing point.

【Continuous Time Sequence | 0:04–0:09 | Foam Generation, Large Amounts of Bubbles Rising】
The camera maintains the downward tilt. Fine white bubbles appear where the soap contacts the magma, then the foam continues to expand, gradually covering the surrounding magma.

Transparent soap bubbles continuously bulge out and detach from the churning white foam, drifting towards the helicopter with the rising airflow. Initially only a few scattered ones, then the number increases rapidly, forming a dense bubble group with front-to-back depth.

Bubbles range in size from grapes to basketballs, with thin-film reflections and faint iridescence on the surface, allowing visibility of the volcano and rock walls through the bubble membrane. Rising speeds vary slightly, colliding and deforming with each other, some popping naturally, while more continue to form behind.

The camera continuously observes the approach of the bubbles. The distant volcano is still visible through gaps, while nearby bubbles gradually occupy more of the frame. The white foam on the magma and the transparent bubbles rising into the air are clearly distinguished.

【Continuous Time Sequence | 0:09–0:13.5 | Bubbles Arrive, Flooding into Cabin】
Bubbles rise to the height of the cabin door, swept up by the rotors and airflow around the fuselage. Some pop or deviate, while more continuously flood in from outside the side door.

The camera follows the bubbles continuously lifting, smoothly turning back into the cabin, refocusing on the man. Shooting position and door frame direction remain consistently aligned, cannot suddenly change to an external view.

The man holds a fixed handle with one hand, leans slightly inward, and naturally raises his other hand to shield his eyes from bubbles approaching too closely. He mainly observes the changes before him, not looking at the lens, not performing exaggeratedly, and not speaking.

Bubbles constantly diffuse from the door into the cabin interior, squeezing between seats, the man's shoulders, and the camera. Nearby bubble membranes gently deform and slide, leaving wet white foam on hair, sleeves, and seats after popping. More bubbles immediately fill in, gradually obscuring cabin structures and character outlines.

【Continuous Time Sequence | 0:13.5–0:15 | Cabin Filled with Bubbles, Direct End】
The camera maintains the current cabin perspective, only retreating slightly with the shooter's body.

Large amounts of bubbles have already crowded the door and surroundings of the person, with the man's upper body almost obscured. Bubbles continue to naturally crowd, drift, and pop; through local gaps, dark sleeves and the hand holding the handle can be seen.

End directly here, do not add actions like parting bubbles to reveal face, looking at the lens, or being covered again; no freeze frame, no pull back.

【Sound】
Real rotor sounds and wind noise from the door persist throughout, accompanied by the sound of soap rubbing against the threshold, low rumbling of distant volcanic churning, and subtle dense popping sounds after bubbles enter the cabin. Sound distance changes naturally with camera orientation. No background music, narration, dialogue, or comedy sound effects.

【Key Constraints】
9:16 vertical screen, 15 seconds, one continuous shot throughout, realistic documentary photography texture. Camera always located near the side door inside the same helicopter.

Only one giant pink soap, which does not reappear in the man's hands after being thrown. Bubbles first generate from the volcano, then continuously rise to the door and flood into the cabin, cannot appear out of nowhere. No single giant bubble wrapping the helicopter.

Transparent bubbles have clear thin-film structures, white foam consists of fine bubbles, avoid depicting as smoke, cotton, or snow. Only use the last 1.5 seconds to show the state where the man's upper body is almost obscured by bubbles, then end immediately. No subtitles, logos, or watermarks.

description: A detailed prompt for generating a 15-second cinematic wuxia combat video with specific camera angles, character consistency, and physics-based action choreography.
promptText:
I. Core Positioning

Generate a strictly 15-second, 16:9 horizontal, 24fps, cinematic realistic quality Chinese Xianxia hard-core combat short film.

Overall Style:

Pure ancient Chinese Xianxia hard-core combat aesthetics
High tension, strong rhythm, extremely clear spatial relationships
Sudden bursts, violent collisions, instant stops
Audiences can only catch the action in moments but never lose orientation
Absorb King Hu's martial arts space and editing essence without replicating any specific movie
Arri Alexa cinema camera texture
Stable sharp facial micro-details
Fine film grain
Natural volumetric lighting
Realistic motion blur
Restrained effects, no light pollution

The core thrill of this short comes from:

Distance suppression of long weapons vs short weapons
Halberd's multi-functional threat: 'thrust, hook, line control, body impact'
Senior sister is suppressed in the first two segments
Third segment completes counterattack by borrowing momentum, actively closing distance, and dismantling the halberd head's effective attack axis
Clear readable geographical orientation and weapon attribution even during high-speed cuts

Do not shoot the combat as:

Soft dance routines
Effect stacking
Random teleportation
Unreadable chaotic fighting
Mechanical fragmented cuts

II. Character Identity Anchors

Lock character identities based on the 1st and 2nd uploaded reference images in order.

Character ID A | 1st Reference Image | Sword Immortal Senior Sister
Always maintain the same person:
East Asian female, 25-30 years old
Oval face
Fair natural skin tone
Dark apricot eyes
Black hair half-tied up
Fixed with white jade hairpin
Tall slender build
Same set of white embroidered silk Hanfu
Semi-transparent layered wide sleeves
Silver waistband
Jade pendant
White cloth boots
One silver straight sword
Sheath retained throughout and can participate in actions
Personality:
Calm
Fast judgment
Clean movements
No showmanship
Every change has a clear tactical purpose

Character ID B | 2nd Reference Image | Junior Sister
Always maintain the same person:
East Asian female, 20-25 years old
Round lively face
Black hair braided
Petite build
Same set of cyan-green linen Hanfu
Dark belt
Wooden hairpin
Black cloth shoes
One dark steel sword
Function:
Never joins the fight
Witnesses from afar
Shocked by the battle
Ends with a restrained breath, no explanatory dialogue

Character ID C | Enemy Halberdier
Same adult East Asian male
Wearing deep iron-grey ancient martial attire
Experienced, stable, fast-reacting
Clearly has real combat experience
Can judge, learn, and correct on the fly
Actually suppresses senior sister in first two segments
Not a toolman standing still to take hits

Character ID D | Elder Master
Same elder master
Always witnesses from afar
Never intervenes
Only calmly delivers one comment at the end

III. Enemy Weapon Design | Long-handled Halberd
Enemy weapon is a cinematically designed long-handled halberd based on ancient halberd structure.
Must retain features:
Front spike
Side branch blade
Clear long handle structure
Can thrust directly
Can hook horizontally
Can control opponent's weapon lines
Can use handle for short, heavy body impacts
Performance Focus:
Segment 1: Use front spike direct thrust to establish long-range threat
Late Segment 1: Use side branch to hook into silver sword line, dragging senior sister's path away
End Segment 1: Use handle height/weight for close-range impact
Segment 2: Continuously complete thrusts, low hooks, reverse impacts, close-line control
End Segment 2: Halberd side branch hooks onto senior sister's deliberately offered sheath mouth
Segment 3: Senior sister borrows force from this 'hook', dismantling halberd head's effective axis
Only one halberd in entire film; design, size, direction, grip stable throughout.

IV. Environment DNA
All newly uploaded background/location reference images are used ONLY as background/location references.
Before formal composition, silently integrate compatible elements:
Real terrain
Architectural language
Spatial scale
Material age
Vegetation
Water bodies
Weather
Mountain mist
Main light direction
Reflection relationships
Air depth
Reasonable combat routes
Recombine into a new space unique to this round but consistent and credible with all references.
Environment Rules
Must maintain:
Real location
Walkable space
Reasonable combat routes
Stable main light direction
Stable geographic relationships
Clear foreground/midground/background layers
Background always naturally alive:
Wind continuously moves hems, hair, vegetation
Water flows naturally
Mountain mist drifts slowly
Reflections/wet surface highlights change subtly
Distant figures have slight natural activity
Background always narratively neutral:
Does not create opportunities actively
Does not collapse or trip people suddenly
Does not block either side
Does not decide victory/defeat
Only when characters truly:
Step on
Collide with
Brush against environment
Move ground or objects
Then local effects appear:
Dust
Ripples
Debris
Leaf displacement
Passive fabric movement

V. Camera Principles
Overall Language
Three clear narrative segments: 0-5s, 5-10s, 10-15s
Approximately 6-7 functional internal cuts total
Each cut triggered ONLY by:
Real impact
Sudden reversal of movement direction
Weapon blocking lens
Body imbalance
Halberd head or sword blade sweeping past lens
Prohibited:
Mechanical average cutting
Causeless fragmented cuts
Handheld shaking throughout
Showy orbiting
Excessive slow motion
Fast flying shots
Gamified cameras
Motion Principles
Actions must have:
Clear weight
Clear inertia
Clear initiation
Clear impact
Clear stop
Allow very short silence after each burst to let danger land.

VI. 15-Second Three-Segment Combat Structure
Shot 1 | 0-5s | Long Halberd First Suppression
Framing & Photography
Wide/Long shot
0.0-1.0s Use 24mm fixed extreme wide shot
Clearly show distance, direction, escape routes
Junior sister and master visible in distance but not distracting
Visual Content
Same white-robed Sword Immortal Senior Sister stands forward.
Only one same deep iron-grey Halberdier directly ahead.
Same cyan-robed Junior Sister and same Elder Master remain distant witnesses.
0.0-1.0s All static, forming pressure.
Then enemy suddenly thrusts along centerline without warning.
Immediately hard cut to low angle 28mm, halberd tip piercing violently through foreground.
Same white-robed immortal dodges with explosive diagonal step at last moment.
But enemy does not stop.
Halberd side branch immediately hooks horizontally into her silver sword's motion line, forcibly dragging sword path away.
Next, enemy uses long handle for one extremely short, extremely heavy body impact, knocking her entire body off balance by a full position.
Both abruptly stop.
No posing.
No extra performance.
Segment Goal
Let audience clearly know:
Enemy is strong
Halberd threat is real
Senior sister gained no advantage in previous segment
Spatial relationship fully understandable

Shot 2 | 5-10s | Halberd Lock Re-suppression, Senior Sister Sets Counter Conditions
Framing & Photography
Medium/Cowboy shot
35mm close photography
Retain continuous pressure as much as possible
No frantic fragmented cuts
Action Content
Maintain:
Same white-robed Sword Immortal
Same Halberdier
Same silver sword
Same long halberd
Fully continuous spatial relationship
Enemy continues continuous pressure:
Upper thrust
Retract halberd body to low hook
Immediately use handle for reverse impact
Senior Sister suddenly explosively closes distance for first time.
Enemy reads her tactic.
He immediately shortens grip, turning long weapon into compact close-control, sealing her entry again, proving he judges and adapts.
Then enemy launches skilled side branch lock again.
This time, Senior Sister does NOT send silver sword in.
She deliberately offers EMPTY SHEATH into attack line.
Halberd side branch accurately hooks sheath mouth.
Retain very short half-beat.
Enemy mistakenly thinks he successfully controlled her second time, pulls back violently.
Segment Goal
Complete necessary premise for third segment counter:
Enemy believes he locked her again
Clear hooking relationship between halberd and sheath
Senior Sister has actively prepared 'borrowing momentum' conditions

Shot 3 | 10-15s | Borrow Momentum, Close Distance, Throat Seal
Framing & Photography
Start with Extreme Close-up
Enter 50mm impact shot after action
Finalize on 85mm extreme close-up
Action Content
Same white-robed Sword Immortal does NOT confront enemy's pulling force head-on.
Instead, she explodes forward with momentum.
While closing distance to enemy, she rotates hooked sheath, changing angle around halberd side branch.
Action must be clearly readable:
She is not brute-force grabbing halberd
She is changing halberd head's effective attack axis
Making entire halberd head temporarily lose space for continued thrust/hook
Long handle sweeps across entire lens, creating natural weapon-blocking cut.
Next 50mm impact shot:
She has closed into enemy's personal space,
Using shoulder for one short, violent impact, disrupting opponent's body axis.
Meanwhile, same silver straight sword remains freely held in other hand.
She spins over enemy's front shoulder following imbalance direction.
Silver sword does not do fancy rotations.
Directly completes one extremely short forward push

title: Skincare Product Commercial Video Prompt
description: A prompt for generating a clean, bright beauty commercial video featuring a Southeast Asian woman demonstrating a skincare routine with specific products.
promptText:
A bright, clean beauty commercial of a young Southeast Asian woman with fair glowing skin, dark hair pulled neatly back, wearing a simple white camisole, standing in a modern bathroom with pastel mint and peach tiled walls, a round gold-rimmed mirror, and a white marble counter. Soft natural lighting, fresh and airy aesthetic, high-end skincare ad look.
She smiles at the camera while holding a light-blue Wardah Lightening Gentle Wash tube. Cut to close-up of her hands on the marble counter picking up a Wardah Lightening Serum dropper bottle among other matching light-blue tubes and a cream jar. She pulls the dropper out with a drop of serum falling. Then she gently pats the lightweight serum onto her cheek with her fingertips, skin looking dewy and radiant. Next she holds a Wardah Lightening Day Cream jar, unscrews the white lid, and applies a small amount of white cream to her face with a glowing finish. Final shot: she stands behind the full product lineup arranged neatly on the counter (Gentle Wash tubes, serums, day cream jar, toner) with both hands framed under her chin, smiling softly.
Cinematic beauty commercial style, shallow depth of field, soft highlights on skin, clean product packaging in matching powder-blue and white, no text overlay, photorealistic, 9:16 vertical.

title: Seedance 2.0 Photorealistic Skincare Ad Prompt
description: A detailed video generation prompt for Seedance 2.0 to create a 10-second vertical photorealistic skincare commercial. It specifies a multi-scene storyboard including unboxing, product hero shots, texture close-ups, and hand movements, emphasizing cinematic lighting and brand consistency.
promptText:
Create a high-quality photorealistic 10-second vertical 9:16 skincare commercial using the uploaded image as the exact visual reference. Preserve the fictional “Cheng Guang Cocoa Soft Glow” bottle design, label, colors, packaging, and overall composition accurately. Do not copy real-world Vaseline trademarks.

Scene 1 (0–2s): Smooth cinematic camera push-in toward the open gift box. The Cheng Guang Cocoa Soft Glow bottle is beautifully revealed among soft pink wrapping paper and decorative elements. Warm cozy lighting, subtle sparkles.

Scene 2 (2–4s): A woman's hands gently pick up the Cheng Guang bottle from the box. Slow natural hand movement, realistic skin texture, soft warm lighting, premium unboxing feeling.

Scene 3 (4–6s): Hero product shot. The bottle stands upright surrounded by cocoa beans, cocoa butter and fresh green leaves. Camera slowly moves from left to right with elegant cinematic depth of field.

Scene 4 (6–7s): Extreme close-up of a smooth lotion texture being spread gently across skin. Show the creamy, lightweight texture and glossy moisturizing finish in realistic macro detail.

Scene 5 (7–9s): The bottle is held elegantly in one hand and slowly rotated toward the camera. Highlight the Cocoa Butter and Serum-in-Lotion concept with premium beauty-commercial lighting.

Scene 6 (9–10s): Final hero shot of the Cheng Guang Cocoa Soft Glow bottle surrounded by cocoa beans and leaves. Camera slowly pushes in, subtle sparkling effects, luxurious warm background, clean product-focused composition.

Style: photorealistic, premium beauty advertisement, cinematic lighting, realistic hand movements, smooth camera transitions, shallow depth of field, soft bokeh, warm golden tones, 4K, highly detailed, natural motion, no distortion, no extra products, no change to bottle label or branding.

Sound

Sword Immortal Sister answers in an extremely solemn tone, as if reporting sect secrets in the main hall:

"Control sword for hundred miles, protect formation and break evil."

The interviewer shows no emotion, immediately follows up:

The scene is quiet for half a second.
The interviewer in the computer calmly replies:

Ending Frame

title: Seedance 2.0 Mini Xianxia Short Film Prompt
description: A comprehensive prompt for generating a 15-second three-shot Xianxia short film titled 'Writing Defeat' using Seedance 2.0 Mini, featuring complex character interactions and moral tension.
promptText:
Seedance 2.0 Mini | 15-second three-shot Xianxia short film prompt | "Writing Defeat"

I. Task Objective

Generate a complete continuous 15-second Chinese Xianxia movie short film, 16:9 landscape, strict three-shot structure, each segment about 5 seconds.

Overall Tone:

Cinematic realistic texture
Pure ancient Chinese Xianxia aesthetic
Mature wartime moral tension
Restrained but constantly taut emotional power
Veteran screenwriter-style dialogue driven by subtext and consequences
Advanced wuxia character scheduling
Arri Alexa cinema camera texture
Stable sharp facial micro-details
Natural volumetric light
Fine film grain

Core reversal revolves around a harder kind of courage:

When continuing to fight for the word "win" will cause more ordinary people to die, does a truly responsible person dare to personally write "defeat" under everyone's gaze?

II. Reference Images and Character Anchors

Character Identity Anchors

Strictly use the 1st image in upload order and 2nd image in upload order as character identity anchors for the two protagonists.

Character ID A | 1st Image | Sword Immortal Senior Sister

Always maintain same person:

25–30 year old East Asian female

Oval fair face
Dark almond eyes
Black hair half-up
Fixed with white jade hairpin
Tall slender figure
Same set of white embroidered silk Hanfu
Silver waist seal
Jade pendant
White cloth boots
Holding same silver long sword
Character ID B | 2nd Image | Junior Sister

Always maintain same person:

20–25 year old East Asian female

Round lively face
Black braided hair
Petite figure
Same set of green linen Hanfu
Dark belt
Wooden hairpin
Black cloth shoes
Holding same dark steel sword
III. Environment DNA and Spatial Principles

All background and location reference images newly uploaded in this round jointly determine the same set of Environment DNA.

Before formal composition, silently reorganize and unify the following content:

Real terrain

Architectural language

Spatial scale
Materials
Vegetation
Water bodies
Weather
Mountain mist
Cloud layers
Reflections
Main light direction
Air depth
Then replan a new location unique to this round, completely unified, real and credible.
General Environment Rules

Background must always be vibrant, but narratively absolutely neutral:

Wind exists naturally continuously

Water flows continuously

Mountain mist wanders according to terrain
Vegetation responds naturally to wind
Clothes and hair naturally affected by wind
Reflections and distant views continuously subtly change
Distant characters and spatial environmental sounds continuously exist
But these environmental elements:
Cannot actively create plot

Cannot help anyone make decisions

Cannot drive conflict resolution
Cannot steal dramatic focus
IV. Plot Structure
Shot 1 | 0–5s

Shot Size

Full shot or long shot

Screen Scheduling

Sword Immortal Senior Sister and Junior Sister located in main foreground area

One enemy commander directly ahead

One elder master, two sect disciples, several wounded civilians, small number of enemy soldiers distributed in different depth layers

Geographic relationship clear and stable
Camera restrained and stable, clearly establishing all character relationships and prop positions
Key Props
A ceasefire document
A brush pen

Table or equivalent ancient writing support surface

Plot and Dialogue
Enemy commander unfolds ceasefire document publicly, says:
"Admit defeat, troops stand down tonight. Don't admit, fight again at sunset."

Master answers coldly:

"There is no surrender character under my tutelage."

Same Junior Sister doesn't argue, only silently reaches out to pick up brush pen on table.

Key Point of This Shot

First layer of conflict established between "admitting defeat" and "sect dignity"

Junior Sister picking up brush action must be steady, slow, clear

Let audience begin to anticipate she will make a decision contrary to expectations

Shot 2 | 5–10s
Shot Size
Medium shot or cowboy shot

Continuity Requirements

Keep following content stable throughout:

Same two protagonists

Same clothing

Same ceasefire document

Same brush pen

Completely consistent geographic space
Supporting character positions continuous
Plot and Actions
Junior Sister writes her own name on ceasefire document in front of everyone.
Master suddenly shouts:
"With this stroke, do you know what you leave behind?"

Junior Sister doesn't look up, only answers:

"I know."

Complete pause for half a beat, then drops one sentence:

"Leaving tomorrow."

Same Sword Immortal Senior Sister suddenly reaches out, takes brush pen from her hand.

In this moment, screen must cause clear misjudgment for audience, thinking Senior Sister wants to stop her, or even might scratch out name.

Next second, Senior Sister extremely calmly writes her own name below Junior Sister's name.

Master truly stunned, asks:

"You also admit defeat?"

Senior Sister answers:

"Defeat is ours."

Pause another beat, then says again:

"Name cannot just leave her alone."

Behind shallow depth of field, enemy commander's originally cold hard expression changes noticeably for first time.

Key Point of This Shot

Junior Sister's writing must be decisive, cannot hesitate too much in performance

Senior Sister's snatching brush action must be restrained, creating one clean misleading moment

Double signature is visual establishment point of core reversal in this film

Dramatic focus on "joint responsibility", not "stopping" or "sentimentality"

Shot 3 | 10–15s
Shot Size
Close-up or extreme close-up
Continuity Requirements

Keep following content stable throughout:

Same Senior Sister

Same Junior Sister

Same ceasefire document

Brush, ink traces, long sword and clothing consistent

Supporting character positions and spatial relationships continuous

Plot and Dialogue
Same Junior Sister looks at Senior Sister, lowers voice asking:
"Senior Sister, aren't you afraid of being laughed at by posterity?"
Same White-robed Sword Immortal truly meets her gaze, only answers:
"Afraid."

Completely retain one clean, weighty pause.

Then she shifts gaze to those injured ordinary civilians, only says:

"First let today's people live until posterity."

Ending Actions and Aftermath

Junior Sister's originally constantly tense expression finally extremely lightly relaxes

Enemy commander silently collects signed ceasefire document

He turns and orders soldiers to lower weapons

Same elder master not easily persuaded, nor makes summary

He only after long silence, slowly steps aside one pace

Final Shot Emotion
Finally two women stand side by side:
No victory posture
No shame expression
They lost a nominal win/loss

They actively preserved next day

V. Performance Principles

Sword Immortal Senior Sister
Restrained
Sober
Doesn't shout slogans

Emotions held very steady

True strength reflected in "actively sharing defeat name"

Junior Sister

Front section silently bears pressure
Middle section firm when writing
Back section emotional loosening extremely light
No crying/shouting, no sentimentality, don't act fragile
Master

Intense but restrained

Not pure villain, nor immediately persuaded
His silence and final concession must carry sense of cost
Enemy Commander
First half treats "admitting defeat" as humiliation

Second half realizes for first time opponent is saving lives for more people

Expression changes clear, but cannot steal protagonist spotlight
Group Supporting Cast
Only witnesses

Maintain natural existence in different depth layers

Don't steal dialogue, don't steal camera dominance
VI. Camera and Photography Requirements
16:9 Landscape

Strictly three continuous clear shots

Camera movement stable, restrained, clear
No showing off techniques
Camera serves character relationships and prop logic

Foreground, middle ground, background maintain real parallax

Let audience clearly see brush, ceasefire document, writing, double signature, supporting character reactions

Lighting and Texture
Natural volumetric light
Fine film grain
Stable sharp facial micro-details
Ink traces, paper, silk clothes, metal weapons must have real texture
VII. Sound and Audio-Visual Sync
Must natively synchronize Mandarin dialogue and precisely match lip movements.

Key sounds include:

Brush writing sound
Paper rustling
Ceasefire document being touched and collected sound
Fabric fine sound

Long sword and scabbard slight metal sound

Environmental wind sound, water sound, distant crowd slight movement

Sound Principles:

Environmental sound continuously naturally exists

Doesn't overpower dialogue
Pauses must have real dramatic weight
When signing and collecting ceasefire document, sound should be clear but restrained
VIII. Seedance 2.0 Mini Execution Focus
For Seedance 2.0 Mini, focus on enhancing following four capabilities:
Multi-person visual primary/secondary clear
Subjects always Senior Sister and Junior Sister
Group cast only witnesses and pressure sources

Action design simple and clear
Picking up brush, writing, snatching brush, signing again, collecting document, conceding
Every action must be readable, cannot be ambiguous

Character identity and core prop continuity
Two protagonists' identities stable
Ceasefire document, brush, ink traces, long sword continuous stable
Supporting character positions as stable as possible
Restrained micro-performance and lighting continuity
Complete emotions via eye contact, pauses, breathing, finger subtle changes
Don't rely on exaggerated performance

title: 1980s Nostalgic Summer Vacation
description: An incredibly detailed documentary-style prompt for Seedance 2.5 to recreate a nostalgic 1985 Japanese summer day through a home video lens.
promptText:
[Overview] A day in the life of a 10-year-old boy spending his summer vacation at his grandparents' rural home in 1985. A young uncle visiting home records with a handheld video camera from a distance without speaking. 480p, 16:9, 15 seconds. 7 shots (approx. 2s each) with hard cuts; all 7 locations are different. No transitions or fades. The subject does nothing for the camera: no eye contact, no showing objects, no waving, no posing. Immersed in play. Fragments cut from the middle of daily life, not acting. No dialogue, lines, or narration.

[Subject] Definition of beauty: A Japanese boy of child-actor caliber whom everyone says will be handsome in the future. A child's face the moment they enter water is best. Face: short black hair with bedhead, thick eyebrows, sharp double-lidded eyes, peeling skin on the bridge of the nose from sunburn (realistic skin texture), white teeth, a small scab on the chin. Clothing (everyday wear): white tank top (slightly yellowed from washing), green shorts, straw hat (frayed brim), white towel around the neck, bare feet in rubber sandals. Habits: pushing the hat back, glancing at the younger brother. Face, hair, and clothing are identical in all shots.

[Characters] Younger brother (6 years old): round face, buzzed head, white tank top and red shorts. Mimics everything the older brother does. Easily scared. No one looks at the camera.

[Era, Place, Light] Rural countryside in August 1985. 1) Veranda of an old Japanese house (morning light, thin smoke from a green coil mosquito repellent, rice with raw egg) 2) Rice field path (midsummer white light, bicycle) 3) Shallow river (sparkling water surface) 4) River rocks (jumping from a small rock to the shallows) 5) On a riverbank stone (watermelon, strong sunlight) 6) Tree in a shrine precinct (dappled sunlight, cicadas) 7) Veranda in the evening (sparkler firework: a small ball of fire sparking at the end of a thin paper twist. Blue twilight). No signs or text in the frame.

[Camera] 1985 home video camera texture: bleeding colors, low resolution, blown-out highlights on water reflections, soft outlines. No date display. Handheld, natural shake, imperfect composition, hunting zoom, exposure fluctuations. 3-6m distance from subject. Subject ignores the camera. No stabilization, gimbals, drones, slow motion, cinematic lighting, or commercial color grading. The camera is always at the height of a person holding it (standing, sitting, crouching, walking, next seat). No angles from places a person couldn't be. The filmer is a person clearly in the same space, following slightly late when the subject moves, occasionally with soft framing.

[Shots] (Approx. 2s each. Each line = Location & Light / Activity / Inner emotion and small leaked gestures / Camera position)
1. Veranda/Morning. Hurriedly eating rice with egg. Eyes already on the garden ahead. Emotion: Wanting to get to the river fast. Mosquito coil smoke drifts sideways. Camera: From outside the veranda.
2. Path/Bicycle. Standing to pedal with the brother on the back. Mouth set in a firm line looking ahead. Emotion: Reliable older brother vibe. Hat slips back in the wind. Camera: Following from behind, shaking.
3. Shallows. Submerged to the waist with a net, holding breath staring at fish. Emotion: Concentration. Brother still behind. Camera: From the bank, water reflections blown out.
4. Rocks. Diving from a small rock into the shallows, laughing loudly with face rising from splashing water. Emotion: Sense of liberation, refreshment. Camera: Slightly away from the bank, spray hits the screen.
5. Bank stone/Watermelon. Biting in, spitting seeds far, glancing at the brother with a smirk. Emotion: Competitiveness. Camera: From the side, strong sunlight.
6. Shrine tree/Dappled light. Thrusting a cicada caught in a net in front of the brother, laughing at him recoil. Emotion: Mischievousness. Camera: From behind the brother.
7. Veranda/Evening. Staring seriously at the fire ball of a sparkler, watching the spot it vanished after falling. Emotion: Small loneliness at the end of the day. Camera: Sitting at the edge of the veranda from the side. During this, at approx 00:14, the recording suddenly blacks out. No fade out.

[Prop Details] Net has a bamboo handle with green mesh. Bicycle is a black utility bike with a carrier. Straw hat brim is frayed. Watermelon is striped, eaten close to the rind. Mosquito coil is a green spiral in a ceramic pig holder. Sparkler has red paper at the tip of the twist.

[Prohibition of Text] No readable text, logos, signs, labels, or numbers on screen.

[Physics & Consistency] Real-world physics. No extra fingers, fused hands, distorted anatomy, floating objects, vanishing items, or sudden deformations. Splashes, wet hair/clothes, and sparks should be realistic. Feet grounded. Hat, towel, and brother's clothes same in all shots.

[Sound] Only natural ambient sounds (switches per shot): clinking of a rice bowl, bicycle chain and wind, river flow, splash of diving, biting watermelon, cicada chorus, crackling of sparklers. No words. Occasional small laughter/breaths from the filmer and subject allowed. No music, no narration, no artificial sound effects.

[Atmosphere] A record of a nondescript day of a boy in Showa-era countryside that makes adults feel 'I had a summer like this.' Fragments of play, not acting. Nostalgic, bright, deeply human. Prioritize the feeling that a camera just happened to be there.

title: UGC Skincare Selfie Vlog

promptText: Create a 15-second, 16:9, 24fps ultra-photorealistic skincare UGC selfie video. REFERENCE PRIORITY Image 1 = exact character identity. Image 2 = exact product appearance. Additional storyboard images = composition, timing and motion only. Keep the woman’s exact face, freckles, skin tone, blue-green eyes, long light-brown caramel hair, blue hoop earrings, pearl necklace, white linen shirt, body proportions and identity consistent throughout. Use Image 2 as the exact Crème de la Mer Moisturizing Cream reference. Preserve the same creamy-white jar, lid, shape, proportions, material, label layout and packaging colors throughout. Never turn it blue, translucent, gel-like, or replace it with another product. STYLE Authentic end-of-day skincare vlog filmed by the woman herself on a smartphone. Relaxed, intimate, slightly tired, low-energy and unperformed. Not a polished beauty ad. No presenter behavior, exaggerated reactions, product-selling gestures or glossy TVC lighting. LOCATION Mediterranean-style villa bedroom at golden hour. White stucco walls, rumpled white bedding, open doorway, soft bougainvillea and olive leaves in the background. Warm natural sunlight enters from frame-left, creating soft golden highlights on her hair, cheek and jaw. No ring light or studio lighting. CAMERA Horizontal 16:9 selfie composition. Keep her face visually dominant, usually 40–60% of frame width. Use asymmetric framing with the product, applying hand or environment on the opposite side. Mostly head-and-shoulders or tight upper-chest framing. Authentic smartphone footage: arm’s-length handheld camera, small tremor, subtle horizontal drift, minor framing corrections, occasional autofocus shifts, mild wide-angle distortion, natural motion blur, slight rolling shutter, subtle sensor noise. Never feel gimbal-stabilized or professionally operated. SHOT 1 — 0:00–0:04 Horizontal selfie close-up. Her face is slightly right-of-center. She pushes loose hair away with the back of her wrist and briefly checks herself on the phone screen. The OPEN white La Mer jar casually enters the lower-left beside her cheek. Natural autofocus shift between face and jar. She exhales softly. Dialogue: “Okay. Last thing, then bed.” SHOT 2 — 0:04–0:07 Horizontal detail shot. Show realistic deformation: dense, silky, opaque cream folds under the finger and forms a soft peak when lifted. Briefly show the front label clearly: “CRÈME DE LA MER™” “LA MER” “moisturizing cream” Then she rubs a small amount between two fingertips. Natural rack focus: label → cream → fingertips. Dialogue: “It’s so rich.” SHOT 3 — 0:07–0:11 Return to horizontal face close-up. Her face slightly left-of-center, applying hand on the right. She warms the cream and gently presses small amounts onto both cheeks, forehead and chin. Do not create a thick white mask. The cream appears briefly, then gradually absorbs. Freckles, pores, under-eye shadows and fine skin texture remain visible. Only a subtle hydrated sheen develops. Dialogue: “I just warm it up and press it in.” SHOT 4 — 0:11–0:15 Closest three-quarter selfie framing. She presses two fingertips into her cheek, lifts them, then slowly turns into the warm sunlight. A subtle hydrated sheen catches the cheekbone while freckles and pores remain visible. She looks mostly at her phone screen, gives a tiny delayed half-smile and small nod. The white La Mer jar appears naturally in soft focus near the lower frame. She reaches toward the phone to stop recording, causing a slight natural sideways tilt. Dialogue: “Morning me is gonna be so happy.” PERFORMANCE End-of-day energy: relaxed, slightly tired, casual and natural. Include subtle micro-behaviors: slow blinking, small exhale, natural swallowing, tiny head tilt, eyes checking the screen, loose hairs falling across her cheek, small posture shifts, delayed half-smile. VOICE Soft female voice, slightly tired and flat. Close smartphone microphone sound. Natural breathing. No studio-clean voice-over. SKIN REALISM Pore-level realism. Visible freckles, pores, fine forehead texture, faint under-eye shadows, tiny imperfections, vellus facial hair, moist eyes, natural catchlights, real lip texture. The moisturizer must behave like a real thick cream before absorbing. No plastic skin, beauty-filter smoothing, artificial glow or waxy face. STRICT NEGATIVE No face drift. No character replacement. No hairstyle or outfit change. No packaging change. No blue jar, blue lid, blue cream or translucent gel. No Laneige or other skincare product. No product duplication. No fake label. No commercial presenter pose. No ring light. No glossy ad lighting. No extreme beauty retouching. No plastic skin. No watermark, subtitles, UI or random text.

title: Alien Planet Found-Footage Vlog
description: A found-footage style prompt of a woman exploring an alien coast, featuring on-camera lines and raw, atmospheric visuals.
promptText: [STYLE + CAMERA + ATMOSPHERE] Real found-footage phone vlog on an alien planet. She is filming as she walks, the way someone records a trip for a friend: uneven clips, hard cuts, the phone too close, then swung out at whatever just moved. Slight shake, bad exposure, soft focus, lens dirt, wind slamming the mic, then creatures and plants filling the frame. When she speaks to the lens, she says the exact short lines written below, clear and plain, in a normal speaking voice. Wind can sit under the words. It does not replace them. No transitions, no slow-mo, no grade, no text, no stickers. It feels raw because the planet is doing too much for a phone. A giant moon hangs in the sky the whole day, pale and huge, even with the suns up. [SUBJECT] A woman about 27 in alien years, off-world traveler filming her own vlog. Cool lilac-grey complexion, faint mint freckles, a short glassy hair-crest messy from wind, gold eyes. Simple field clothes the whole take: dusty linen wrap, travel shirt, boots, a small pack. Fully clothed in every clip. She talks to the lens only at the beats marked below, then forgets the camera and points it at the planet. Same face in every cut. Calm, curious, a little worn. Not performing. [PLACE] An alien wild coast, lived-in and too big for the phone. Chalk shelves, forests of tall ribbed plants that lean and creak, ground-cover that pulls back when a boot lands, a gel-river the color of bottle glass, herds crossing open amber flats, a cliff path under the giant moon. Two small suns. Wind, grit, insect-choir, distant animal calls. No postcard town. The extraordinary stuff is just outside the lane. [ON-CAMERA LINES] She only speaks these lines, in this order, in a clear everyday voice: 1. “Day two. That moon still hasn’t moved.” 2. “It’s fine. It’s just eating.” 3. “They cross here every day. Look at the legs.” 4. “Yeah. I’m not going in.” 5. “Two suns. Moon’s still up.” 6. “Stopping here. I’ll send this later.” [TIMELINE — PHONE VLOG, HARD CUTS] 0-4s: HOOK — she is already walking a chalk shelf, phone in her hand, giant moon filling the upper frame behind her. She turns the lens on herself and says, clear: “Day two. That moon still hasn’t moved.” Then she flips the phone out: a stand of ribbed plants as tall as towers, swaying, seed-pods knocking. Raw, immediate. 4-9s: She pushes through a lane of vegetation. Leaves the size of doors fold aside and settle behind her. Cut to the phone dropped low: ground-cover peeling back from her boots, pale roots clicking. Cut to her stopping, holding the phone steady, filming a slow six-legged grazer the size of a cart chewing a pod. It looks at the lens. She does not get closer. She says, clear, off the side of the frame: “It’s fine. It’s just eating.” Wind under the line, words intact. 9-15s: She crests a rise. The giant moon sits on the horizon, enormous, craters readable. She films it, then the phone dips and catches a herd of long-necked grazers crossing the amber flat, legs too many, moving like a slow traffic jam. Cut to a close of a plant opening as the herd passes, then shutting. Cut to her face for a second, squinting. She says, clear: “They cross here every day. Look at the legs.” Then the phone goes back to the animals. Overexposed, dusty, real. 15-21s: Gel-river. She stands on the bank and films the surface beading and rolling upstream. Something large moves under it, a dark shape, then a fin of shell breaks and sinks. She steps back, laughs once, and says, clear: “Yeah. I’m not going in.” Cut to her crouched, filming a cluster of cube-bodied river birds pecking the mud. One hops onto a rock and stares. She stays quiet. Cut to the moon reflected, broken, in the gel. Phone almost slips. She catches it. 21-26s: Afternoon wind. She follows a dirt track between breathing shell-boulders. A door-sized beetle crosses ahead and she waits, filming its legs, then its eye, then the plants it brushes. She stays quiet. Cut to her wiping the lens with her sleeve. Cut to a high shelf: two suns, the giant moon still up, a valley of moving forest below. She turns the lens on herself and says, clear: “Two suns. Moon’s still up.” Then she holds the wide shot. The audio is wind, the far call, and that line. 26-30s: The light drops. The moon brightens until it is the main light. She films a night-opening grove, pods glowing faint mint, small flyers stitching between them. Cut to her face, tired, hair-crest flat from the wind, the moon over her shoulder. She says, clear: “Stopping here. I’ll send this later.” Last shot: phone pointed out from the shelf at the giant moon and the dark gel-river, a herd still moving as small shapes, her breathing on the mic, then the recording ends mid-step, like a real vlog file. [REALISM LOCK] Found footage alien vlog only. Handheld phone, hard cuts, dirty lens, wind, bad exposure. Same woman, fully clothed, same face. She speaks only the six written lines, in order, intelligible, everyday English. Giant moon in the sky all day. Creatures and vegetation carry the clips: ribbed forest, ground-cover that pulls back, a six-legged grazer, a many-legged herd, cube-bodied river birds, a shape under the gel, a door-sized beetle. Raw, specific, extraordinary, and ordinary to her.

title: Dark Gothic Psychological Horror Mirror Scene
description: A detailed narrative prompt for Seedance 2.5 depicting a psychological horror encounter between a jester and her reflection, with precise choreography and atmospheric details.
promptText: HALF A BEAT LATE — 15 seconds. Dark gothic psychological horror. 16:9. Real-time action, controlled cuts, continuous spatial and emotional progression. REFERENCES Image 1 defines adult female jester Sin and her identical evil mirror double: exact face, white makeup, red nose, dark eye makeup, painted tear marks, red twin-horn hair, gold crown with bells, ivory ruff, red-and-blue court costume, pointed shoes. Image 2 defines the room and opening frame: burgundy curtain and warm wall sconce on the left, charcoal walls, wooden floor, large antique gold mirror on the right. Preserve the room, mirror frame, and light direction. IDENTITY AND STAGING SIN starts outside the mirror: increasingly frightened, resisting capture. DOUBLE starts inside the mirror: amused, disobedient, smiling, physically assertive. After the exchange, DOUBLE is outside in the room and SIN is trapped behind intact glass. Begin on Image 2’s empty-room composition. Sin enters from lower-left, walks diagonally to the mirror, and stops about 55 cm from the glass, torso facing it, back and partial profile toward camera. Keep her slightly off the mirror center so both real and reflected faces stay visible. Camera remains on the mirror’s left-front side; the glass stays broadly visible, not edge-on. Natural perspective, readable facial detail, enough depth of field for both faces. During the exchange, Sin passes inward through the screen-left half of the mirror while Double steps outward through the screen-right half. Their paths stay separate. Afterward Double takes one short settling step toward screen-left, ending in the left foreground while trapped Sin remains visible inside the mirror on the right. PERFORMANCE LOCK Sin stops smiling once she notices the anomaly and never smiles again. Double keeps smiling and never copies Sin’s fear. Sin shakes her head, retreats, gasps, loses balance, resists. Double refuses to follow, advances, grips, pulls, plants its feet. After the exchange, Sin panics inside the mirror while Double turns toward camera, smiles wickedly, then whispers. Both faces stay alive and natural, never frozen or deformed. 0-3 SECONDS — THE SMILE REMAINS A heel clicks offscreen. Sin enters immediately, takes two or three short grounded steps to the mirror, relaxed posture, chin slightly raised, small habitual smile. Weight transfers naturally through each foot; skirt and crown bells follow with soft motion and sound. Her reflection appears normal at first. Sin briefly adjusts the side of her crown with her right hand, lowers it, exhales, and her mouth turns neutral. The reflected hand lowers about half a second late. Double keeps smiling and slowly shows its teeth. A restrained push-in keeps both faces readable: Sin neutral and unsmiling, Double still smiling. 3-5.5 SECONDS — OPEN DISOBEDIENCE Sin looks from Double’s mouth to its eyes, brow tightening, then slowly shakes her head once. Double does not shake. It tilts its head slightly and widens its amused smile. Sin catches her breath, draws her chin back, retreats about 20 cm, and raises her right hand at chest height, palm toward the mirror. Double leans closer to the glass as Sin increases her real distance. Keep both opposing movements visible in the same oblique frame. 5.5-8 SECONDS — GRIP, THEN PULL Hard cut to a same-side medium shot holding both faces, Sin’s raised right wrist, and the mirror’s left edge. A localized patch of glass turns into a dark elastic membrane. Double’s left hand reaches through into the room and grips Sin’s right wrist firmly. Double pulls inward. Sin’s eyes snap to the captured wrist; her lips part in a sharp inhale. Her left hand grabs the mirror’s left frame, rear foot braces on the wooden floor, knees bend as she pulls backward. Double keeps its cold smile and retracts with steady force. Sin loses her hold on the frame. Her right shoulder is pulled forward first, then her torso; her rear shoe begins to slide. She resists the whole time and never walks voluntarily into the mirror. 8-11.5 SECONDS — ONE IN, ONE OUT The camera withdraws slightly to reveal the mirror boundary and landing foot. Double steps outward through the screen-right half of the mirror and plants one pointed shoe firmly on the wooden floor before taking weight. Sin is pulled inward through the screen-left half. Double keeps hold until Sin crosses the surface, then releases her wrist. Their identical faces pass on separate paths: Sin terrified, trembling, ragged breath; Double composed with a small victorious smile. Red hair and moving fabric briefly occlude the crossing point. Use one concealed continuity cut inside that occlusion only. When the occlusion clears, the exchange is complete: inside the mirror Sin stumbles one step away, then turns and lunges back toward the glass; outside, Double completes its settling step toward screen-left. The membrane seals back into intact reflective glass before Sin reaches it. Her palms hit the inner surface and stop. The gold frame stays rigid. No shattering. 11.5-13 SECONDS — TURN FIRST Hard cut to a same-side medium close shot that clearly contains both faces. Double starts facing the mirror, then shoulders and torso turn toward the camera until its face is fully visible. Show the full body turn before any frontal smile. Behind it, trapped Sin faces outward from inside the mirror. She looks down at her blocked palms, urgently scans the frame edges, then looks at Double. She strikes the glass once and opens her mouth to call out, unheard. Sin remains an independent trapped person, not a synchronized reflection. 13-14 SECONDS — THEN THE EVIL SMILE Double finishes turning and stands still, shoulders relaxed, eyes on the lens. Only now does one corner of its mouth rise into a clearly wicked, satisfied smile with a little tooth visible. Keep Sin sharply readable behind it: raised inner brows, tense lower lids, downturned mouth, fast chest movement, palms pressed to the glass. Her fear continues throughout Double’s smile. 14-15 SECONDS — FINALLY, “SHH” Double raises its right index finger to its lips, slightly gathers its smile, and whispers directly to camera: “Shh.” The voice is low, intimate, steady. Sin strikes the glass again with one hand while the other stays planted, mouth open in a silent plea. She never mirrors the finger gesture, smile, or gaze. Hard cut to black at exactly 15 seconds. COLOR AND LIGHT Single consistent palette: charcoal brown #211E1B for walls and deep shadow, dark burgundy #4B171A for curtain and red costume shadow, aged brass #9C7544 for mirror frame, crown, and bells, ivory grey #D8D0C1 for makeup and ruff, deep blue-grey #29313B for blue costume fabric and cool shadow. Preserve Image 2’s warm left-side sconce at about 2700-3000K. Localized old-gold highlights, subtly cool shadows, neutral midtones, restrained saturation, dense textured blacks. Protect the white makeup from orange or blue contamination. Mirror glare never hides the reflected face. No color, exposure, or lighting reset during the exchange. AUDIO Heel clicks, fabric movement, and delicate bells establish the room. Sin’s interrupted breath builds into gasps during resistance. Add wrist-grip friction, shoe scrape, frame contact, and restrained membrane tension. After the mirror seals, Sin’s voice and breathing are inaudible from the room; her impacts become faint muffled thuds. Double’s final “Shh” is the only spoken line. No music, narration, or subtitles. CONTINUITY LOCKS Exactly one original Sin and one evil Double. Preserve separate identities, correct wrist ownership, grip contact, resistance, and inward/outward travel paths across cuts. No merged bodies, duplicate occupants, extra hands, or position jumps. Before the anomaly, the reflection behaves naturally. After the exchange, both performances remain independent. Camera: From the next seat, dark outside. Around 00:14, the recording suddenly cuts to a blackout. No fade out.

[Text Prohibition] No readable text, logos, signs, labels, packages, screen displays, or numbers anywhere on screen. The can is plain. Replace objects that might have text with plain versions.

[Sound] Natural ambient sounds only (switching per shot): silence of the room, sound of the belt at the entrance, leaves in the park, sound of the river, clock in the room, cars under the footbridge, train running sound. No words at all. Occasional small laughs and breathing from the filmer and subject are allowed. No music. No narration. No artificial sound effects.

[Atmosphere] A record of an ordinary day of a Reiwa-era Jirai-kei girl that makes one think 'there's a girl like this.' Not acting, but fragments caught by chance. Cute, a bit lonely, and deeply human. Prioritize the feeling that the camera just happened to be there.
